The Petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act 1989, claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents with regard to the death of her son Sri. D. N.
Manjunath S/o late Narayanappa, in the road traffic accident that took place on 25-10-2023.
2. The brief facts of the petition are as follows:
It is the case of the Petitioner that, on 25-10-2023 at about 8.30 p.m., the deceased was driving the TATA Ace bearing Reg. No. KA-53-AA-4798 proceeding on Chinatamani - Hosakote SH-82 road, Bengaluru Rural district, slowly and cautiously observing all the traffic rules and regulations, when he reached near K. Sathyawara gate, at that time Tata Ace bearing Reg. No. KA-53-B- 4541 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering to human life, came at high speed and dashed to the deceased vehicle and caused the accident. Due to sudden impact,
deceased sustained several grievous injuries on vital parts of the body. 
Immediately after the accident he was shifted to Hosakote Government hospital. The duty doctors examined and declared brought dead. Thereafter, the post mortem was conducted and after Venkatamma vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 19 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160317905/
2 conducting post mortem the Petitioner had shifted the dead body to her native place and performed the last rites and obsequies ceremony and spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards funeral expenses. 
On account of the sudden and sad demise of the deceased in the said accident, the Petitioner was undergoing deep mental shock, pain and suffering and hardship. 
Prior to the accident the deceased was hale, healthy and was aged about 30 years and he was working as a Driver and earning Rs.20,000/- per month. The Petitioner being the mother of the deceased, has lost love and affection and undergoing great mental shock and mental agony. 
The respondent No.1 is the Insurer of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay Rs.50,00,00,000/- with cost and interest to the Petitioner. Hence, prayed to allow the petition. 
3. After service of notice, the Respondent No.1 to 3 have appeared through their respective Counsels and filed the written statements. 
The Respondent No.1 filed the written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and denied the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle. This respondent has issued the policy in-respect of the Tata Ace No.KA-53-B-4541 and policy was in-force and liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy. The driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving license to drive the said vehicle on the date of accident. This respondent further submitted that, the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the deceased, as he was negligent in driving his TATA Ace in the middle of the road in a Zig zag manner without taking any precautionary measure and lost control over his vehicle and dashed against the offending vehicle. 
Further, this respondent also denied the age, occupation and income of the deceased. By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. 
The Respondent No.2 filed the written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and denied the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle. This respondent admitted that he is the R.C. Owner of Tata Ace No.KA-53-B-4541 and contended that, the said vehicle is insured with respondent No.1. The D.L. to drive the said vehicle and Insurance policy were in force as on the date of accident, hence respondent No.1 has to indemnify the respondent No.2 and pray to dismiss the petition. The Respondent No.3 filed the written statement by admitting the averments of the petition in part and contended that, Petitioner is the Mother and she is the wife of the deceased Sri.
D. N. Manjunath. Further submitted that, at the time of accident, deceased was earning Rs.25,000/-
p.m. along with Batta of Rs.200/- per day. Further contended that, after completion of Postmortem examination the dead body was handed over to the Petitioner and to this respondent. Further submitted that, after the death of her husband there was some misunderstanding arose between the Petitioner and this respondent, as such the petitioner has not impleaded this respondent as Petitioner in this petition. The Petitioner's intention is to grab the entire death benefit and the petitioner is harassing this respondent by taking innocence of this respondent. During the life time of her husband, he was taking care of this respondent by providing food, clothes and other basic necessities for her livelihood. Hence, prays to allow the petition and prays to apportioned the 3rd respondent's share of compensation.

3 4. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following issues:
1) Whether the Petitioner proves that on 25- 10-2023 at about 8.30 p.m., accident took place on Chintamani - Hosakote SH-82 Road,
K.Sathyawara gate, Bengaluru Rural District, due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Tata Ace No.KA-53/B-4541 as a result her son has succumbed to the accidental injuries? 
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, how much? 
3. What order or award? 
5. In order order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to 13. On the other hand, inspite of granting sufficient time, the respondents not adduced the evidence. 
6. Heard the arguments on both the sides and perused the material placed on record.
7. My findings on the above issues as under:-
Issue No.1 ... In the affirmative, Issue No.2 ... Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.3 ...
As per final order, for the following:
:REASONS:
8. ISSUE No.1: The petitioner contended that on 25.10.2023 at about 8.30 p.m. deceased D. N.
Manjunath met with road traffic accident due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Tata Ace bearing Reg. No. KA-53-B-4541.
9. The petitioner is the mother of the deceased. The petitioner in order to establish this case filed the affidavit in lieu of chief examination of PW-1 and reiterated the petition averments and got marked the documents at Exs.P.1 to 14.
10. Negligence is a specific tort and in any given circumstances, the failure to exercise that care which the circumstances demand, where there is a duty to exercise care, reasonable care must be taken to avoid acts or omissions which can be reasonably foreseen to be likely to cause physical injury to persons or property. In order to succeed in an action for damages/ compensation for breach, the aggrieved must establish breach of statutory duty which on the construction of the statute. It is well settled that, those who claim negligence have to prove on the probabilities, as to whether breach or negligence, has caused or materially contributed to the damage suffered by the claimant/s.
11. The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person. It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence Venkatamma vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 19 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160317905/
4 to shameful disregard of safety of others. In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act. 
Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something. In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do. 
12. The burden is upon the petitioners to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent driving of the driver of the Tata Ace bearing Reg. No. KA-53-B-4541 .
13. As we know evidence in any Summary Proceedings, " The act of Negligence" will have to be assessed on the basis of broad preponderance of probabilities and degree of proof required is not one of beyond reasonable doubt, as it is insisted in criminal case for " The Negligent Act ". 
14. As per the case of the petitioners, it could be seen that on 25-10-2023 at about 8.30 p.m., the deceased was driving the TATA Ace bearing Reg. No. KA-53-AA-4798 proceeding on Chinatamani - Hosakote SH-82 road, Bengaluru Rural district, slowly and cautiously observing all the traffic rules and regulations, when he reached near K. Sathyawara gate, at that time Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.
KA-53-B-4541 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering to human life, came at high speed and dashed to the deceased vehicle and caused the accident. Due to sudden impact, deceased succumbed to the accidental injuries. Accordingly, the Hosakote Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.279/2023. After completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 279 and 304(a) of IPC.
15. The certified copy of the First Information (First information statement/s complaint in common para-lace) lodged before the Hosakote Traffic Police has been marked as Ex.P.2. On receiving the First Information, the Station House Officer chose to register a case in Crime No. 279/2023. The said certified copy of First Information Report (F.I.R.) is marked as Ex.P.1.
16. During the Course of examination-in-chief, petitioner/she got marked Ex.P.1 is the FIR, Ex.P.2 is the complaint, Ex.P.3 is the Charge sheet, Ex.P.4 is the Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.5 is the Death Intimation, Ex.P.6 is the Sketch, Ex.P.7 is the IMV Report, Ex.P.8 is the Inquest Report, Ex.P.9 is the Postmortem Report, Ex.P.10 is the Notice u/s 133 of M.V. Act, Ex.P.11 is the Reply notice,
Ex.P.12 is the Notarized copy of Aadhar Card, Ex.P.13 is the copy of Aadhar card of deceased and Ex.P.14 is the copy of Driving License of deceased. Ex.P1 to 4 are the only documents, which are to be scrutinized to arrive at conclusion- whether the accident was owing to the negligent manner of driving by the Tata Ace vehicle driver. The Ex.P.4 (spot panchanama) and Ex.P.6(sketch) clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Information, held investigation and filed the Ex.P.3, Charge-Sheet against the driver of the Tractor U/s. 279 and 304(A) of IPC. The Ex. P.7 i.e. , certified copy of the IMV Report discloses that, the accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle in question. 
17. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR Venkatamma vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 19 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160317905/
5 (CIVIL)
319.
18. The respondents have not stepped into the witness box to rebut the evidence of petitioner and to support the defence taken up in the written statement that the deceased also contributed his own negligence towards the occurrence of the accident in question. In the light of not entering into witness box an adverse inference will have to be drawn as contemplated Under Sec.114 (g) of the Indian Evidence Act that the defence taken in the written statement is not true and correct. 
19. In view of the detailed discussion held above, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner has proved negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle and as such the accident in question had taken place. By relying on evidence of PW.1 and the Police records, I am of the considered view that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Tata Ace bearing Reg. No. KA-53-B-4541 and resulted in death of deceased D. N. Manjunath . Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative. 
20. ISSUE No.2: This issue is regarding dependency, quantum of compensation to be awarded to petitioners and who is liable to pay the same, which is answered under the following heads:
21. LOSS OF DEPENDENCY: To ascertain the actual loss of dependency, the age, income of deceased and the number of dependents of the deceased are to be taken into consideration. It is the contention of the petitioners that they are solely depending upon the income of the deceased and due to death of D. N. Manjunath, they have lost love and affection of the deceased. 
22. The petitioner is the mother of the deceased. Fact to be noted here that petitioner is none other than the mother of the deceased is not seriously disputed by the contesting respondent. Even there is no material on record to show this dependent has independent income of her own and thereby not depended on deceased at all, the deceased out of his income contributed to the income of family consisting of himself and petitioner herein. It is further contended that, the respondent No.3 is the wife of the deceased. Though PW.1 in her cross-examination deposed that, her deceased son and respondent No.3 i.e., wife of deceased son are residing with her but she further stated that, before the accident she left her son. She also deposed that, she has not attended the funeral ceremony of her son and since 02 years she don't know where she reside. Though learned counsel for petitioner contended that, she is not depending upon the income of the deceased. Further he also contended that, though she appeared before this court and she left the petitioner 02 years back. The above discussion makes it clear that, atleast before the accident both mother and wife are depending upon the income of the deceased. Further, in objections respondent No.3 contended that, petitioner has not taken any care of her after the death of her husband. During the life time of her husband, he was taking care of her . Further she also contended that, at the time of postmortem examination of deceased D. N. Manjunath she was present and also received the dead body of her husband along with petitioner. Further she admits that, there was some misunderstanding arose between the petitioner and herself. Though in this case, respondent No.3 not stepped into the witness box but there is no dispute between the relationship between petitioner and respondent with the deceased Venkatamma vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 19 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160317905/ 
6 D. N. Manjunath. Further, it is admitted fact that, atleast prior to the death of deceased D. N.
Manjunath petitioner and respondent No.3 are residing with deceased D. N. Manjunath. Hence, it is clear that, petitioner and respondent No.3 are depending upon the income of the deceased D. N.
Manjunath. Hence, 1/3 is to be deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased. 
23. In a decision reported in 2018 ACJ 5 (Hem Raj Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd., & Others),
Wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court held that, "there can not be distinction where there is evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guesswork, as such addition on account of future prospects is admissible where in the absence of proof of income". 
24. The petitioners contended that, at the time of accident, the deceased was aged 30 years and working as Driver and earning Rs.20,000/- per month. The petitioners have produced the postmortem report of deceased D. N. Manjunath which is marked at Ex.P.9. On perusal of the Ex.P.12 Notarized copy of Aadhar Card, age of the deceased is mentioned as 30 Years as on the date of accident. The accident took place in the year 2023. It is stated by PW.1 that, prior to an accident the deceased was working as Driver and thereby he got income of Rs.20,000/- p.m., but no reliable evidence is produced by the petitioner to show how much income he was getting from his work. So,
in the absence of any evidence in respect of the income of the petitioner, the petitioner might have monthly income at Rs.16,000/- as per the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed notional income of the year 2023 at Rs.16,000/- per month for determination of income before Lok-Adalat for the Districts coming under the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru Bench. The accident is of the year is 2023. Hence, the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/-p.m. as per above decision. 
25. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in decision reported in Civil appeal No.19-20/2021 dated:
05.01.2021, in the case of Keerthi and others V/s Oriental Insurance company ltd., has also observed that, Hemaraju V/s Oriental Insurance company Ltd., decisions puts at rest, any argument concerning non-payment of future prospects to the present case, we are of the view that, there cannot be distinction where there is positive evidence of the income and where minimum income is determined on guess work in the facts and circumstances of the case. Both the situation stands at the same fitting. Hence, the income of the deceased is the Tribunal has to consider the future prospects on actual salary less tax and even for self employed or were engaged on fixed wages. 
Considering recent judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Special leave petitioner (Civil No.25590/2014 dated:31.10.2016 (National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi &
Others), in which it is observed that, "in case if the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary,
an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years. An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation". So 40% of future prospects is taken into consideration. Taking into consideration of the same, if 40% is added to the income of the deceased it would be Rs.16,000/- + 40% (Rs.6,400/-) = Rs.22,400/- per month. There are 2 dependents. Hence, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal expenses. So, 1/3rd of Rs.22,400/- would be Rs.7,466/-. 
Income for consideration (Rs.22,400-7,466) is Rs.14,934/- per month. Therefore the annual income Venkatamma vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 19 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160317905/
7 (Rs.14,934 x 12) is Rs.1,79,208/-. As such correct multiplier as per guidelines of Sarala Varma case would be "17". Thus the loss of dependency works out to (Rs.1,79,208/- x 17) is Rs.30,46,536/-. 
26. TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY, FUNERAL EXPENSES AND LOSS OF ESTATE: The petitioners have spent the amount towards shifting the dead body and performing funeral and obsequies ceremony. In this regard, the Hon'ble Supreme Court judgment passed in Special Leave petitioner (Civil) No.25590/2014 dated:31-10-2017 (National Insurance Co., Ltd Vs.
Pranaya Sethi and Others), wherein it is held that as far as conventional heads are concerned, the petitioners are entitled for funeral expenses of Rs.15,000/- and under the head of loss of estate at Rs.15,000/-. 
27. LOSS OF CONSORTIUM: The counsel for petitioners relied on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil appeal No.9581/2018 (Arising out of SLP(Civil) No.3192/2018) in case of Muama General Insurance co. Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others. 
In which it is held in para No.8.7 that:
"A constitution bench of this court in pranay sethi (supra) dealt with the various heads under which the compensation it so be awarded in a death case. One of these heads is "Loss of consortium". 
In legal parlance "consortium" is a compendious term which encompasses spousal consortium; parental consortium and filial consortium. 
The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance,
solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family. With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse. 
Spouse consortium is generally defined as rights pertaining to the relationship of a husband-wife which allows compensation to the surviving spouse for loss of "company", society, co- operation, affection and aid of the other in every conjugal relation".
Parental consortium is granted to the child upon the premature death of a parent, for loss of "parental aid, protection, affection, society, discipline, guidance and training".
Filial consortium is the right of the parents to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child. An accident leading to the death of a child causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased. The greatest agony for a parent is to lose their child during their lifetime. 
Children are valued for their love, affection, companionship and their oral in the family unit.

8 Consortium is a special prism reflection changing norms about the status and worth of actual relationship. Modern jurisdictional world-over have recognized that the value further on perusal of child's consortium far exceeds the economic value of the compensation awarded in case of death of a child. Most jurisdictions therefore permit parents to be awarded compensation under loss of consortium on the death of a child. The amount awarded to the parents is a compensating for loss of love, affection, care and companionship of the deceased child. 
28. The petitioner is the mother of the deceased and respondent No.3 is the wife of the deceased, so they are entitled for consortium for loss of "protection, affection, society, discipline, guidance and training". Therefore, Rs.40,000/- each is awarded to the petitioners No.1 and respondent No.3 under the head of loss of consortium. 
29. Considering the above facts and for the above reasons, the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads:
1 Loss of dependency Rs.30,46,536/-
2 Loss of consortium Rs. 80,000/-
3 Towards transportation of dead Rs. 15,000/-
body and funeral expenses 4 Loss of estate Rs. 15,000/-
Total Rs.31,56,536/-
Hence, this Tribunal feels to award just and proper compensation of Rs.31,56,536/-
to the petitioners. 
30. LIABILITY: As discussed in issue No.1, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Tata Ace bearing Reg. No. KA-53-B-4541 and the police have conducted due inquiry and filed charge sheet against the driver of said offending vehicle. On perusal of the policy, the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent No.1 for the period from 30.06.2023 to 29.06.2024. Admittedly, the accident in question took place on 25.10.2023. Hence, policy was inforce as on the date of accident. Hence, in view of above discussion, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. However, respondent No.1 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.2 owner. 
31. INTEREST: As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied In a decision in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co.Ltd 2018 ACJ 5 (Hem Raj Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd., & Others), wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%. Accordingly, ISSUE No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative. 
32. ISSUE NO.3: In view of above discussion and findings, I proceed to pass the following:

9 ORDER The petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs. 
The petitioners are entitled for a compensation of Rs.31,56,536/- with interest @ 6%
per annum from the date of petition till the date of payment. 
The respondent No.1 and 2 are liable to pay compensation to the petitioner with interest. The respondent No.1 being insurer is liable to deposit the amount before Tribunal within two months from the date of this order. 
After deposit of compensation amount, 70% share is apportioned infavour of the petitioner and 30% share is apportioned infavour of respondent No.3 respectively. 
Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner and respondent No.3, 50%
shall be deposited as FD in their names in any nationalized or schedule bank for a period of three years and remaining 50% balance amount with accrued interest shall be released to the petitioner and respondent No.3 on proper identification. 
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon, disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No. 2/2019 dated 19.8.2019. 
The petitioner is hereby directed to produce particulars of their Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contains compulsorily photograph of petitioners and respondent No.3,
which is duly attested by concerned Bank. Further petitioner and respondent No.3 shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card. 
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest, the petitioner and respondent No.3 are entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal. 
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission by the Tribunal. 
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
Draw award accordingly.

"A constitution bench of this court in pranay sethi (supra) dealt with the various heads under which the compensation it so be awarded in a death case.
One of these heads is "Loss of consortium".
In legal parlance "consortium" is a compendious term which encompasses spousal consortium; parental consortium and filial consortium.

The petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner and respondent No.3, 50%
shall be deposited as FD in their names in any nationalized or schedule bank for a period of three years and remaining 50% balance amount with accrued interest shall be released to the petitioner and respondent No.3 on proper identification.

which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner and respondent No.3 shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.

In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest, the petitioner and respondent No.3 are entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.

Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission by the Tribunal.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
Draw award accordingly.
